jobs.title: Program Director - Healthy Steps
jobs.description:
Overview

The earliest years of a child’s life create the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and emotional well-being. At Brookdale Hospital, the HealthySteps Program Director has the opportunity to shape that foundation by leading an innovative, evidence-based program that integrates child development and infant mental health expertise directly into pediatric primary care.

The Program Director provides the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership necessary to ensure that infants, young children, and their families receive coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate support in pediatric primary care. The Program Director leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees program quality and fidelity, staff development, grant administration, fiscal performance, clinical operations, data and outcomes reporting, and community partnerships.

HealthySteps, a nationally recognized program of ZERO TO THREE, strengthens the traditional pediatric care model by addressing the developmental, behavioral, social-emotional, and family needs that influence a child’s ability to thrive. HealthySteps at Brookdale Hospital is supported by public and private funding and participates in a multisite, statewide initiative funded by the New York State Office of Mental Health to expand and integrate mental health services within pediatric primary care.

Through collaborative leadership and a commitment to health equity, the Program Director advances Brookdale Hospital’s ability to give children and families—particularly those from historically under-served communities—the strongest possible start in life.

Responsibilities

Leadership and Staff Supervision:

Provide administrative and reflective supervision to a multidisciplinary team of seven (7) staff representing varying disciplines and credential levels, as well as assigned interns and volunteers.
Assign and adjust staff responsibilities to promote operational efficiency, appropriate workload distribution, and maximum delivery of HealthySteps services.
Oversee the HealthySteps’ pediatric residency training program, including curriculum development, delivery, and evaluation.
Establish performance expectations, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, and address performance or conduct concerns in collaboration with Human Resources and departmental leadership.

Grant Management

Lead the development, submission, administration, and renewal of public and private grant applications, continuation requests, and related funding proposals.
Serve as the primary program liaison to funding organizations and ensure compliance with grant requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and reporting deadlines.
Prepare and submit accurate and timely program progress, outcome, financial, continuation, and closeout reports.
Maintain appropriate documentation to support grant monitoring, audits, and program reviews.
Identify potential funding opportunities and collaborate with organizational leadership on strategies to promote program sustainability and expansion.

Budget And Fiscal Management

Develop and manage the HealthySteps operating and grant-funded budgets, including personnel, contractual, and program-related expenditures.
Monitor expenditures against approved budgets and grant line items.
Collaborate with Finance and departmental leadership to prepare budget projections, reconcile expenditures, and address anticipated variances.
Recommend budget modifications and reallocations, when necessary, subject to organizational and funder approval.
Ensure responsible stewardship of public and private program funds.

Program Oversight

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the implementation, maintenance, and continued development of the HealthySteps program.
Ensure fidelity to the HealthySteps model, including participation in national reporting, fidelity monitoring, technical assistance, and site self-assessment activities.
Establish, monitor, and evaluate program goals, workflows, performance measures, service-delivery standards, and patient outcomes.
Oversee program evaluation, data collection, data integrity, and clinical documentation standards.
Ensure the timely and accurate submission of departmental, organizational, regulatory, and funder reports.
Ensure program operations comply with applicable federal and state regulations, grant requirements, organizational policies, professional standards, and patient privacy requirements.
Identify opportunities for performance improvement and lead corrective action and quality-improvement initiatives when appropriate.
Collaborate with pediatric providers and other members of the interdisciplinary care team to support coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate care.

Organizational And Community Collaboration

Coordinate with hospital departments and clinical programs to address the needs of patients, families, program staff, and community partners.
Participate in and lead special projects, hospital-wide initiatives, and cross-departmental activities, including quality improvement and care-coordination initiatives related to maternal and child health.
Represent HealthySteps and Brookdale Hospital at community meetings, coalitions, professional forums, funding meetings, and partnership activities.
Develop and maintain effective relationships with community-based organizations, government agencies, healthcare providers, educational institutions, and other stakeholders.
Advocate for accessible, culturally responsive, trauma-informed services for infants, young children, and their families.
Perform other related duties consistent with the position’s responsibilities and necessary to support the successful implementation and sustainability of the HealthySteps program.

Qualifications

Education:

Master’s Degree in psychology, social work, or counseling from an accredited college or university, required.
Doctoral degree in psychology, counseling, social work, infant mental health or related discipline, preferred.

Experience

Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in program administration, clinical program operations, or project management, required.
Minimum of two (2) years of supervisory or management experience, including responsibility for staff development and performance management, required.
Experience working in a healthcare, pediatric, behavioral health, integrated primary care, or community-based clinical setting, preferred.
Experience administering grant-funded programs, including performance monitoring and preparation of grant or funder reports, preferred.
Demonstrated experience working with infants, children under three years of age, parents, caregivers, and families, preferred.
Experience assessing or supporting infant and early childhood growth, development, social-emotional functioning, and parent-child relationships, preferred.

Licenses/Certifications

Current and valid New York State license as a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) or Licensed Psychologist required.
License must be in good standing and maintained throughout employment with OBH.

New York State Infant Mental Health endorsed, preferred.

Knowledge And Skills

Excellent oral and written communication skills, including grant writing, funder reporting and clinical documentation.
Advanced knowledge of infant and early childhood development, infant mental health, parent-child relationships, family systems, and developmentally appropriate interventions.
Advanced knowledge of reflective supervision principles and the demonstrated ability to apply them in a multidisciplinary clinical environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, motivate, and evaluate multidisciplinary teams representing different professional disciplines and credential levels.
Knowledge of integrated pediatric primary care, family-centered care, trauma-informed practice, and culturally responsive service delivery.
Ability to interpret grant requirements and translate them into measurable program objectives, workflows, and staff responsibilities.
Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and report program quality, utilization, and fidelity data.
Working knowledge of budget development, expense monitoring, financial projections, and fiscal reporting.
Strong interpersonal, presentation, facilitation, and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and respond effectively to changing program needs.
Ability to establish productive working relationships with patients, families, clinical teams, funders, community partners, and organizational leadership.
Demonstrated commitment to serving culturally diverse and medically or economically underserved populations.
Proficiency with electronic health record systems, data-reporting platforms, and standard office productivity software.

Physical Requirements

Position requires prolonged periods of sitting, standing, reaching, and walking throughout the working day.
Position requires travel between main hospital and ambulatory care sites.
Position will be required to stoop, bend, lift, and carry items weighing up to 25 pounds.

jobs.title: CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER (CEO)
jobs.description:
Job Description

CEO/General Manager

Gem City Market – Dayton, Ohio

Retained Search Partner: The Carlisle Group

Salary Range: $90,000 – $115,000

The Carlisle Group is pleased to be partnered on a retained search with Gem City Market
in Dayton, Ohio, in the search for their next CEO/General Manager
.

Gem City Market is a community-centered, full-service grocery cooperative created to bring quality, affordable food to a diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood in Dayton. More than simply a grocery store, Gem City Market is committed to being a pillar of the community it serves—helping strengthen the local culture, creating opportunity, and providing a welcoming place where neighbors can shop, connect, and thrive.

The co-op is seeking an entrepreneurial, community-minded grocery leader who can balance mission and margin
—someone who understands that a successful cooperative must deliver both meaningful community impact and strong financial performance. The CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to lead the Market into its next chapter while ensuring that customers receive quality products at affordable prices in a clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment.

Living in Dayton

Dayton offers an appealing combination of affordability, accessibility, community, and opportunity
. Located in southwest Ohio, Dayton provides the amenities of a larger metropolitan area while retaining a strong sense of neighborhood and community.

The city has a rich history of innovation, entrepreneurship, and community involvement and is home to a diverse collection of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, parks, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy access to an extensive regional park system, the great Miami River, biking and hiking trails, and numerous opportunities to enjoy the outdoors.

Dayton's location is another advantage. Cincinnati and Columbus are both within approximately an hour's drive, while Cleveland and Indianapolis are accessible within a few hours. The region offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared with many larger U.S. metropolitan areas, making Dayton an attractive place to build both a career and a life.

For a leader who wants to make a tangible difference in a community while enjoying a high quality of life, Dayton presents a compelling opportunity.

Position Purpose

The CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading Gem City Market as a successful, financially sustainable cooperative while advancing the goals and purposes established by the Board of Directors.

The CEO/General Manager Will Ensure That The Market

Operates efficiently and ultimately profitably.
Provides quality, affordable groceries that meet the needs of its customers.
Maintains a clean, welcoming, and inclusive shopping environment.
Builds a positive culture for employees and the broader community.
Advances the cooperative's mission and role as a community institution.
Remains responsive to the needs of the diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood it serves.

The CEO/General Manager will bring together the disciplines of grocery operations, financial management, merchandising, people leadership, marketing, and community engagement
to ensure the continued success of Gem City Market.

Overview Of Responsibilities

Operations

Lead an efficient, customer-focused, and ultimately profitable cooperative grocery operation.
Create a positive store atmosphere and build a motivated, accountable staff team.
Maintain current knowledge of grocery retailing, industry trends, and best practices, particularly those applicable to cooperative markets and urban, low- to moderate-income communities.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with market partners, wholesale distributors, local markets, and other industry resources.
Establish and maintain an appropriate product mix that meets shopper needs while supporting financial objectives.
Develop and execute a margin strategy that allows Gem City Market to remain price competitive while maintaining adequate cash flow.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, licenses, permits, health requirements, and employment standards.
Continuously evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, customer service, and profitability.

Financial Management & Strategic Planning

Develop and recommend long- and short-range plans designed to achieve the cooperative's purposes and strategic objectives.
Direct the financial operations of the cooperative and maintain accountability for the organization's financial performance.
Develop operating, capital, and cash budgets for Board approval and manage the business within approved financial parameters.
Provide regular, meaningful financial and operational reporting to the Board of Directors.
Monitor key grocery industry metrics and use financial and operational data to make informed decisions.
Identify new business opportunities and make recommendations to the Board regarding potential growth, partnerships, and innovation.
Participate in regional and national cooperative and grocery industry events to remain connected to emerging trends and best practices.

People & Culture

Determine the appropriate staffing structure and maintain clear, effective job descriptions.
Hire management personnel and oversee the hiring, training, development, and retention of Market staff.
Create a positive, productive, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.
Manage and evaluate employees while providing timely coaching, feedback, recognition, and accountability.
Establish appropriate compensation structures based upon the budget, local labor market, and competitive conditions.
Organize staffing to promote a fair distribution of work while maintaining excellent customer service.
Develop and maintain an effective employee benefits program.
Build a culture where employees understand the Market's mission and their role in delivering it.

Marketing & Community Engagement

Develop and execute an effective advertising and marketing strategy that maintains strong public awareness of Gem City Market and its products and services.
Ensure marketing activities are executed within established budgetary guidelines.
Communicate effectively with cooperative members, customers, employees, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Prepare or oversee the preparation of the annual report and other communications to the cooperative's members and community.
Ensure that store displays, signage, promotions, and merchandising effectively support sales and customer engagement.
Strengthen Gem City Market's position as a trusted and visible community institution.
Identify opportunities to deepen relationships with local organizations, businesses, producers, and community partners.

Reporting Relationships

The CEO/General Manager reports directly to the Board of Directors
, which includes Market staff and members of the community.

The Board is responsible for establishing the organization's overall direction, goals, and expectations, while the CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading day-to-day operations and executing the strategy established by the Board.

The CEO/General Manager has the authority to hire, direct, structure, develop, and evaluate all other Market staff.

The successful candidate will understand the importance of building a strong, collaborative relationship with the Board based on trust, transparency, accountability, and open communication
.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of grocery retail expertise, financial acumen, leadership ability, entrepreneurial thinking, and a genuine commitment to community.

Grocery Retail Leadership

Minimum of five years of successful experience managing a retail grocery store.
Strong understanding of grocery store operations and the various departments required to achieve sales, margin, labor, and profitability goals.
Demonstrated understanding of key grocery industry metrics and how to use them to drive performance.
Experience managing both retail and administrative functions.
Knowledge of current grocery industry trends and competitive dynamics.
Experience with merchandising and marketing in highly competitive grocery markets.

Financial Management

Demonstrated bottom-line accountability for a grocery or retail operation.
Strong understanding of financial variables and their relationship to overall business performance.
Experience developing and managing operating, capital, and cash budgets.
Ability to analyze financial and operational information and translate it into effective business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to balance affordability and customer needs with margin, cash flow, and profitability requirements.

Leadership & People Management

Proven ability to motivate, lead, and coordinate people to achieve organizational objectives.
Experience hiring, training, evaluating, developing, compensating, and, when necessary, terminating employees.
Ability to establish clear expectations and hold people accountable.
Strong listening skills and the ability to both give and receive constructive feedback.
Self-aware, self-motivated, and comfortable taking ownership of decisions and outcomes.
Ability to handle multiple priorities and demands while maintaining focus on the organization's most important objectives.

Cooperative & Community Leadership

Genuine understanding of and appreciation for the cooperative business model.
Ability to articulate what makes a cooperative different and how cooperative principles influence decision-making.
Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
Ability to build trust with Board members, employees, customers, and community stakeholders.
Service-oriented leadership style with a genuine interest in improving the community served by the organization.
Experience working in a food desert, food-insecure, or low-income community is highly valued.

Strategic & Entrepreneurial Thinking

Ability to make difficult decisions and take appropriate risks when necessary.
Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes and develop practical solutions.
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities for innovation and growth.
Ability to maintain momentum and lead change with a sense of urgency.
Willingness to seek outside expertise and perspectives when appropriate.
Ability to balance immediate operational demands with the long-term health and sustainability of the cooperative.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on grocery leader and community-minded executive
to lead an organization with a purpose that extends well beyond the four walls of a grocery store.

The next CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to strengthen Gem City Market's financial and operational performance while helping fulfill its larger role as a source of affordable food, employment, connection, and opportunity within the Dayton community.

For the right leader, this is more than an opportunity to run a grocery store. It is an opportunity to help build a stronger community through grocery retail.

Interested candidates should contact Brett Myers, Managing Director of The Carlisle Group
, for more information regarding this retained search at bcm@tcgrecruit.com
.

jobs.title: Program Director, Major Accounts & District Partnerships
jobs.description:
At ACT, Your Work Makes a Difference

Education has power – a power that changes lives forever. It creates opportunities that lift up individuals, their families, and sparks societal change that echoes through generations to come. From our grassroots we have fought the good fight for equity in education, and we remain devoted to helping anyone who struggles to access that power. This is what matters to us and we must do better -- we’ve never been more sure of our purpose.

ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable environment in which every team member has an opportunity to grow.

We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. You can find a comprehensive list of our benefits here.

We are seeking a Program Director of Major Accounts and District Partnerships
to help us fulfill that mission.

ACT's largest and most complex district partnerships require a different kind of leader. The Program Director of Major Accounts and District Partnerships
owns a focused portfolio of the nation's largest school districts with responsibility for new business capture, growth within existing relationships, and driving measurable impact at scale. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who knows these districts, has credibility at the leadership table, and can navigate the full complexity of large-district procurement and decision-making.

The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary in the range of $115,000 to $125,000.
ACT manages salaries within the range based on relevant factors including, skills, experience, and internal equity. This position is incentive eligible.

Location:
This is a remote position, based in the United States.
Visa:
Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

What You Will Be Working On

A named account list of approximately 50 of the nation's largest school districts
A plan that identifies, qualifies, and pursues high-value opportunities across assigned accounts, including new solution adoption, expanded utilization, and contract growth with measurable outcomes
Direct engagement with district senior leadership — Superintendents, Associate Superintendents, and Cabinet-level decision makers, and boards of education — to align ACT solutions with district priorities and initiatives
Develop and execute comprehensive, multi-year account plans for each assigned district, working with account and program management teams for account support
Lead ACT's response to large district RFPs — driving solutioning, costing, and requirements development
Navigate complex procurement processes involving multiple stakeholders, funding sources, and budget cycles
Advise districts on post-adoption data utilization and best practices to drive measurable outcomes
Inform internal product, pricing, and delivery decisions based on the unique needs and scale of major districts
Collaborate with state partnership and field sales teams to align on strategy, share intelligence, and coordinate on shared accounts
Represent ACT at national and regional events, building and maintaining a strong presence among large-district leadership networks

This could be the job for you if you have (minimum requirements):

At least 7 years of significant experience selling to or working within large K-12 school districts
Have an established network of senior district leaders, you either have these districts as current or former clients or you’ve held a senior role inside one; ability to influence and engage individuals at the district senior leadership and decision-making level from day one
Deep knowledge of district priorities, budget cycles, funding mechanisms, and procurement processes
Proven track record closing complex, multi-year deals in competitive environments
Command of the K-12 assessment landscape — policy, competitive dynamics, and how districts evaluate and adopt assessment solutions
Elite negotiation, consultative selling, and executive presentation skills
Ability to gather and use competitive intelligence to create strategies that advance and/or protect ACT’s interests
Ability to work effectively and build relationships with individuals within the organization
Strong communication skills including ability to communicate effectively across all levels in the organization
Strong analytical abilities and the ability to determine logical solutions to complicated problems
Ability to set goals and priorities and manage to completion
Access to a central hub airport and ability to travel at least 25% of time
Bachelor’s degree in Education, Business or a related area of study; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

It’s a Plus If You Have

Direct experience with college and career readiness programs, assessments, or related solutions
Familiarity with state-level education policy and how it shapes district decision-making
Experience coordinating across internal teams (product, operations, finance) to structure large, customized deals

About ACT

When ACT was founded in 1959, it disrupted the assessment industry with a new approach to helping students better understand their readiness so they could take steps to improve it. By leveraging our expertise and authority in assessment and research, we will again disrupt the industry—helping more people learn, better measure their progress, and improve their navigation through life’s transitions.

More than ever before, ACT is fulfilling its mission of helping people achieve education and workplace success. We’re doing it by pushing the boundaries of learning innovation through the work of our people, who we call team members because we’re all in this together.

We know transformation does not come without challenge. That’s why ACT invests in a variety of experiences for team members to strengthen their connections, explore ideas, learn from customers, and celebrate success.

Learn more about working at ACT at act.org!

new_jobs.title: Program Director - Healthy Steps
new_jobs.description:
Overview

The earliest years of a child’s life create the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and emotional well-being. At Brookdale Hospital, the HealthySteps Program Director has the opportunity to shape that foundation by leading an innovative, evidence-based program that integrates child development and infant mental health expertise directly into pediatric primary care.

The Program Director provides the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership necessary to ensure that infants, young children, and their families receive coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate support in pediatric primary care. The Program Director leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees program quality and fidelity, staff development, grant administration, fiscal performance, clinical operations, data and outcomes reporting, and community partnerships.

HealthySteps, a nationally recognized program of ZERO TO THREE, strengthens the traditional pediatric care model by addressing the developmental, behavioral, social-emotional, and family needs that influence a child’s ability to thrive. HealthySteps at Brookdale Hospital is supported by public and private funding and participates in a multisite, statewide initiative funded by the New York State Office of Mental Health to expand and integrate mental health services within pediatric primary care.

Through collaborative leadership and a commitment to health equity, the Program Director advances Brookdale Hospital’s ability to give children and families—particularly those from historically under-served communities—the strongest possible start in life.

Responsibilities

Leadership and Staff Supervision:

Provide administrative and reflective supervision to a multidisciplinary team of seven (7) staff representing varying disciplines and credential levels, as well as assigned interns and volunteers.
Assign and adjust staff responsibilities to promote operational efficiency, appropriate workload distribution, and maximum delivery of HealthySteps services.
Oversee the HealthySteps’ pediatric residency training program, including curriculum development, delivery, and evaluation.
Establish performance expectations, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, and address performance or conduct concerns in collaboration with Human Resources and departmental leadership.

Grant Management

Lead the development, submission, administration, and renewal of public and private grant applications, continuation requests, and related funding proposals.
Serve as the primary program liaison to funding organizations and ensure compliance with grant requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and reporting deadlines.
Prepare and submit accurate and timely program progress, outcome, financial, continuation, and closeout reports.
Maintain appropriate documentation to support grant monitoring, audits, and program reviews.
Identify potential funding opportunities and collaborate with organizational leadership on strategies to promote program sustainability and expansion.

Budget And Fiscal Management

Develop and manage the HealthySteps operating and grant-funded budgets, including personnel, contractual, and program-related expenditures.
Monitor expenditures against approved budgets and grant line items.
Collaborate with Finance and departmental leadership to prepare budget projections, reconcile expenditures, and address anticipated variances.
Recommend budget modifications and reallocations, when necessary, subject to organizational and funder approval.
Ensure responsible stewardship of public and private program funds.

Program Oversight

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the implementation, maintenance, and continued development of the HealthySteps program.
Ensure fidelity to the HealthySteps model, including participation in national reporting, fidelity monitoring, technical assistance, and site self-assessment activities.
Establish, monitor, and evaluate program goals, workflows, performance measures, service-delivery standards, and patient outcomes.
Oversee program evaluation, data collection, data integrity, and clinical documentation standards.
Ensure the timely and accurate submission of departmental, organizational, regulatory, and funder reports.
Ensure program operations comply with applicable federal and state regulations, grant requirements, organizational policies, professional standards, and patient privacy requirements.
Identify opportunities for performance improvement and lead corrective action and quality-improvement initiatives when appropriate.
Collaborate with pediatric providers and other members of the interdisciplinary care team to support coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate care.

Organizational And Community Collaboration

Coordinate with hospital departments and clinical programs to address the needs of patients, families, program staff, and community partners.
Participate in and lead special projects, hospital-wide initiatives, and cross-departmental activities, including quality improvement and care-coordination initiatives related to maternal and child health.
Represent HealthySteps and Brookdale Hospital at community meetings, coalitions, professional forums, funding meetings, and partnership activities.
Develop and maintain effective relationships with community-based organizations, government agencies, healthcare providers, educational institutions, and other stakeholders.
Advocate for accessible, culturally responsive, trauma-informed services for infants, young children, and their families.
Perform other related duties consistent with the position’s responsibilities and necessary to support the successful implementation and sustainability of the HealthySteps program.

Qualifications

Education:

Master’s Degree in psychology, social work, or counseling from an accredited college or university, required.
Doctoral degree in psychology, counseling, social work, infant mental health or related discipline, preferred.

Experience

Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in program administration, clinical program operations, or project management, required.
Minimum of two (2) years of supervisory or management experience, including responsibility for staff development and performance management, required.
Experience working in a healthcare, pediatric, behavioral health, integrated primary care, or community-based clinical setting, preferred.
Experience administering grant-funded programs, including performance monitoring and preparation of grant or funder reports, preferred.
Demonstrated experience working with infants, children under three years of age, parents, caregivers, and families, preferred.
Experience assessing or supporting infant and early childhood growth, development, social-emotional functioning, and parent-child relationships, preferred.

Licenses/Certifications

Current and valid New York State license as a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) or Licensed Psychologist required.
License must be in good standing and maintained throughout employment with OBH.

New York State Infant Mental Health endorsed, preferred.

Knowledge And Skills

Excellent oral and written communication skills, including grant writing, funder reporting and clinical documentation.
Advanced knowledge of infant and early childhood development, infant mental health, parent-child relationships, family systems, and developmentally appropriate interventions.
Advanced knowledge of reflective supervision principles and the demonstrated ability to apply them in a multidisciplinary clinical environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, motivate, and evaluate multidisciplinary teams representing different professional disciplines and credential levels.
Knowledge of integrated pediatric primary care, family-centered care, trauma-informed practice, and culturally responsive service delivery.
Ability to interpret grant requirements and translate them into measurable program objectives, workflows, and staff responsibilities.
Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and report program quality, utilization, and fidelity data.
Working knowledge of budget development, expense monitoring, financial projections, and fiscal reporting.
Strong interpersonal, presentation, facilitation, and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and respond effectively to changing program needs.
Ability to establish productive working relationships with patients, families, clinical teams, funders, community partners, and organizational leadership.
Demonstrated commitment to serving culturally diverse and medically or economically underserved populations.
Proficiency with electronic health record systems, data-reporting platforms, and standard office productivity software.

Physical Requirements

Position requires prolonged periods of sitting, standing, reaching, and walking throughout the working day.
Position requires travel between main hospital and ambulatory care sites.
Position will be required to stoop, bend, lift, and carry items weighing up to 25 pounds.

new_jobs.title: CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER (CEO)
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

CEO/General Manager

Gem City Market – Dayton, Ohio

Retained Search Partner: The Carlisle Group

Salary Range: $90,000 – $115,000

The Carlisle Group is pleased to be partnered on a retained search with Gem City Market
in Dayton, Ohio, in the search for their next CEO/General Manager
.

Gem City Market is a community-centered, full-service grocery cooperative created to bring quality, affordable food to a diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood in Dayton. More than simply a grocery store, Gem City Market is committed to being a pillar of the community it serves—helping strengthen the local culture, creating opportunity, and providing a welcoming place where neighbors can shop, connect, and thrive.

The co-op is seeking an entrepreneurial, community-minded grocery leader who can balance mission and margin
—someone who understands that a successful cooperative must deliver both meaningful community impact and strong financial performance. The CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to lead the Market into its next chapter while ensuring that customers receive quality products at affordable prices in a clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment.

Living in Dayton

Dayton offers an appealing combination of affordability, accessibility, community, and opportunity
. Located in southwest Ohio, Dayton provides the amenities of a larger metropolitan area while retaining a strong sense of neighborhood and community.

The city has a rich history of innovation, entrepreneurship, and community involvement and is home to a diverse collection of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, parks, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy access to an extensive regional park system, the great Miami River, biking and hiking trails, and numerous opportunities to enjoy the outdoors.

Dayton's location is another advantage. Cincinnati and Columbus are both within approximately an hour's drive, while Cleveland and Indianapolis are accessible within a few hours. The region offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared with many larger U.S. metropolitan areas, making Dayton an attractive place to build both a career and a life.

For a leader who wants to make a tangible difference in a community while enjoying a high quality of life, Dayton presents a compelling opportunity.

Position Purpose

The CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading Gem City Market as a successful, financially sustainable cooperative while advancing the goals and purposes established by the Board of Directors.

The CEO/General Manager Will Ensure That The Market

Operates efficiently and ultimately profitably.
Provides quality, affordable groceries that meet the needs of its customers.
Maintains a clean, welcoming, and inclusive shopping environment.
Builds a positive culture for employees and the broader community.
Advances the cooperative's mission and role as a community institution.
Remains responsive to the needs of the diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood it serves.

The CEO/General Manager will bring together the disciplines of grocery operations, financial management, merchandising, people leadership, marketing, and community engagement
to ensure the continued success of Gem City Market.

Overview Of Responsibilities

Operations

Lead an efficient, customer-focused, and ultimately profitable cooperative grocery operation.
Create a positive store atmosphere and build a motivated, accountable staff team.
Maintain current knowledge of grocery retailing, industry trends, and best practices, particularly those applicable to cooperative markets and urban, low- to moderate-income communities.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with market partners, wholesale distributors, local markets, and other industry resources.
Establish and maintain an appropriate product mix that meets shopper needs while supporting financial objectives.
Develop and execute a margin strategy that allows Gem City Market to remain price competitive while maintaining adequate cash flow.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, licenses, permits, health requirements, and employment standards.
Continuously evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, customer service, and profitability.

Financial Management & Strategic Planning

Develop and recommend long- and short-range plans designed to achieve the cooperative's purposes and strategic objectives.
Direct the financial operations of the cooperative and maintain accountability for the organization's financial performance.
Develop operating, capital, and cash budgets for Board approval and manage the business within approved financial parameters.
Provide regular, meaningful financial and operational reporting to the Board of Directors.
Monitor key grocery industry metrics and use financial and operational data to make informed decisions.
Identify new business opportunities and make recommendations to the Board regarding potential growth, partnerships, and innovation.
Participate in regional and national cooperative and grocery industry events to remain connected to emerging trends and best practices.

People & Culture

Determine the appropriate staffing structure and maintain clear, effective job descriptions.
Hire management personnel and oversee the hiring, training, development, and retention of Market staff.
Create a positive, productive, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.
Manage and evaluate employees while providing timely coaching, feedback, recognition, and accountability.
Establish appropriate compensation structures based upon the budget, local labor market, and competitive conditions.
Organize staffing to promote a fair distribution of work while maintaining excellent customer service.
Develop and maintain an effective employee benefits program.
Build a culture where employees understand the Market's mission and their role in delivering it.

Marketing & Community Engagement

Develop and execute an effective advertising and marketing strategy that maintains strong public awareness of Gem City Market and its products and services.
Ensure marketing activities are executed within established budgetary guidelines.
Communicate effectively with cooperative members, customers, employees, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Prepare or oversee the preparation of the annual report and other communications to the cooperative's members and community.
Ensure that store displays, signage, promotions, and merchandising effectively support sales and customer engagement.
Strengthen Gem City Market's position as a trusted and visible community institution.
Identify opportunities to deepen relationships with local organizations, businesses, producers, and community partners.

Reporting Relationships

The CEO/General Manager reports directly to the Board of Directors
, which includes Market staff and members of the community.

The Board is responsible for establishing the organization's overall direction, goals, and expectations, while the CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading day-to-day operations and executing the strategy established by the Board.

The CEO/General Manager has the authority to hire, direct, structure, develop, and evaluate all other Market staff.

The successful candidate will understand the importance of building a strong, collaborative relationship with the Board based on trust, transparency, accountability, and open communication
.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of grocery retail expertise, financial acumen, leadership ability, entrepreneurial thinking, and a genuine commitment to community.

Grocery Retail Leadership

Minimum of five years of successful experience managing a retail grocery store.
Strong understanding of grocery store operations and the various departments required to achieve sales, margin, labor, and profitability goals.
Demonstrated understanding of key grocery industry metrics and how to use them to drive performance.
Experience managing both retail and administrative functions.
Knowledge of current grocery industry trends and competitive dynamics.
Experience with merchandising and marketing in highly competitive grocery markets.

Financial Management

Demonstrated bottom-line accountability for a grocery or retail operation.
Strong understanding of financial variables and their relationship to overall business performance.
Experience developing and managing operating, capital, and cash budgets.
Ability to analyze financial and operational information and translate it into effective business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to balance affordability and customer needs with margin, cash flow, and profitability requirements.

Leadership & People Management

Proven ability to motivate, lead, and coordinate people to achieve organizational objectives.
Experience hiring, training, evaluating, developing, compensating, and, when necessary, terminating employees.
Ability to establish clear expectations and hold people accountable.
Strong listening skills and the ability to both give and receive constructive feedback.
Self-aware, self-motivated, and comfortable taking ownership of decisions and outcomes.
Ability to handle multiple priorities and demands while maintaining focus on the organization's most important objectives.

Cooperative & Community Leadership

Genuine understanding of and appreciation for the cooperative business model.
Ability to articulate what makes a cooperative different and how cooperative principles influence decision-making.
Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
Ability to build trust with Board members, employees, customers, and community stakeholders.
Service-oriented leadership style with a genuine interest in improving the community served by the organization.
Experience working in a food desert, food-insecure, or low-income community is highly valued.

Strategic & Entrepreneurial Thinking

Ability to make difficult decisions and take appropriate risks when necessary.
Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes and develop practical solutions.
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities for innovation and growth.
Ability to maintain momentum and lead change with a sense of urgency.
Willingness to seek outside expertise and perspectives when appropriate.
Ability to balance immediate operational demands with the long-term health and sustainability of the cooperative.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on grocery leader and community-minded executive
to lead an organization with a purpose that extends well beyond the four walls of a grocery store.

The next CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to strengthen Gem City Market's financial and operational performance while helping fulfill its larger role as a source of affordable food, employment, connection, and opportunity within the Dayton community.

For the right leader, this is more than an opportunity to run a grocery store. It is an opportunity to help build a stronger community through grocery retail.

Interested candidates should contact Brett Myers, Managing Director of The Carlisle Group
, for more information regarding this retained search at bcm@tcgrecruit.com
.

new_jobs.description:
At ACT, Your Work Makes a Difference

Education has power – a power that changes lives forever. It creates opportunities that lift up individuals, their families, and sparks societal change that echoes through generations to come. From our grassroots we have fought the good fight for equity in education, and we remain devoted to helping anyone who struggles to access that power. This is what matters to us and we must do better -- we’ve never been more sure of our purpose.

ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable environment in which every team member has an opportunity to grow.

We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. You can find a comprehensive list of our benefits here.

We are seeking a Program Director of Major Accounts and District Partnerships
to help us fulfill that mission.

ACT's largest and most complex district partnerships require a different kind of leader. The Program Director of Major Accounts and District Partnerships
owns a focused portfolio of the nation's largest school districts with responsibility for new business capture, growth within existing relationships, and driving measurable impact at scale. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who knows these districts, has credibility at the leadership table, and can navigate the full complexity of large-district procurement and decision-making.

The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary in the range of $115,000 to $125,000.
ACT manages salaries within the range based on relevant factors including, skills, experience, and internal equity. This position is incentive eligible.

Location:
This is a remote position, based in the United States.
Visa:
Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

What You Will Be Working On

A named account list of approximately 50 of the nation's largest school districts
A plan that identifies, qualifies, and pursues high-value opportunities across assigned accounts, including new solution adoption, expanded utilization, and contract growth with measurable outcomes
Direct engagement with district senior leadership — Superintendents, Associate Superintendents, and Cabinet-level decision makers, and boards of education — to align ACT solutions with district priorities and initiatives
Develop and execute comprehensive, multi-year account plans for each assigned district, working with account and program management teams for account support
Lead ACT's response to large district RFPs — driving solutioning, costing, and requirements development
Navigate complex procurement processes involving multiple stakeholders, funding sources, and budget cycles
Advise districts on post-adoption data utilization and best practices to drive measurable outcomes
Inform internal product, pricing, and delivery decisions based on the unique needs and scale of major districts
Collaborate with state partnership and field sales teams to align on strategy, share intelligence, and coordinate on shared accounts
Represent ACT at national and regional events, building and maintaining a strong presence among large-district leadership networks

This could be the job for you if you have (minimum requirements):

At least 7 years of significant experience selling to or working within large K-12 school districts
Have an established network of senior district leaders, you either have these districts as current or former clients or you’ve held a senior role inside one; ability to influence and engage individuals at the district senior leadership and decision-making level from day one
Deep knowledge of district priorities, budget cycles, funding mechanisms, and procurement processes
Proven track record closing complex, multi-year deals in competitive environments
Command of the K-12 assessment landscape — policy, competitive dynamics, and how districts evaluate and adopt assessment solutions
Elite negotiation, consultative selling, and executive presentation skills
Ability to gather and use competitive intelligence to create strategies that advance and/or protect ACT’s interests
Ability to work effectively and build relationships with individuals within the organization
Strong communication skills including ability to communicate effectively across all levels in the organization
Strong analytical abilities and the ability to determine logical solutions to complicated problems
Ability to set goals and priorities and manage to completion
Access to a central hub airport and ability to travel at least 25% of time
Bachelor’s degree in Education, Business or a related area of study; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

It’s a Plus If You Have

Direct experience with college and career readiness programs, assessments, or related solutions
Familiarity with state-level education policy and how it shapes district decision-making
Experience coordinating across internal teams (product, operations, finance) to structure large, customized deals

About ACT

When ACT was founded in 1959, it disrupted the assessment industry with a new approach to helping students better understand their readiness so they could take steps to improve it. By leveraging our expertise and authority in assessment and research, we will again disrupt the industry—helping more people learn, better measure their progress, and improve their navigation through life’s transitions.

More than ever before, ACT is fulfilling its mission of helping people achieve education and workplace success. We’re doing it by pushing the boundaries of learning innovation through the work of our people, who we call team members because we’re all in this together.

We know transformation does not come without challenge. That’s why ACT invests in a variety of experiences for team members to strengthen their connections, explore ideas, learn from customers, and celebrate success.

Learn more about working at ACT at act.org!

ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable environment in which every team member has an opportunity to grow.

We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. You can find a comprehensive list of our benefits here.

We are seeking a Senior Program Director, State Chief Liaison
to help us fulfill that mission.
The Senior Program Director, State Chief Liaison will focus on connecting K-12 Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, and Boards of Education to ACT’s policy-driven strategies that influence revenue and long-term positioning.

The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary in the range of $120,000 to $160,000.
ACT manages salaries within the range based on relevant factors including, skills, experience, and internal equity. The position is incentive eligible.

Location:
This is a remote position, based in the United States.
Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

What You Will Be Working On

Build and maintain relationships with state-level decision-makers (Commissioners, Boards of Education, Deputy Commissioners).
Advise on policy trends and accountability shifts impacting assessment and readiness programs.
Serve as ACT’s policy liaison for executive-level discussions, ensuring ACT solutions align with state priorities.
Influence and guide RFP executive summaries and “model” frameworks to reflect policy priorities.
Provide strategic intelligence on state education policy changes and their implications for ACT’s offerings.
Collaborate with Government Relations (GR) to ensure unified messaging without duplicating lobbying efforts.
Success Metrics:
Overall revenue generation and growth of assigned states (indirect / influence).
Number of quality strategic policy engagements at commissioner/board level.
Influence on RFP language and executive summaries.
Policy-driven opportunities identified and converted into actionable business strategies.
Number of ACT solutions added to state level pathways/requirements.

Role Progression

At the end of 3 months you will have:

Become familiar with ACT products and services and internal/external stakeholders.
Establish relationships across the organization where there are common goals.
Identify states, create a territory map to include decision makers, history and vulnerabilities.

Within 6 Months You Will:

Begin developing strategic initiatives and how to deliver on them.
Identify RFPs and deliver multi-level plans for opportunities to flip states.
Monitor legislation via tracking system and document actions and progress.

Within 9 Months You Will:

Achieve successful outcomes via legislative process and Governor-led initiatives.
Influence RFP language to align with ACT products.
Start seeing tangible results -- additional states using our products and blocking competition.

This could be the job for you if you have (minimum requirements):

At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in education industry.
Experience serving in a leadership role at a State Department of Education, a State Higher Education Executive Officers (SHEEO) agency, or a State Department of Labor, in roles such as Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Assistant Commissioner, Chief of Staff, State Director, or equivalent executive leadership roles.
Demonstrated ability to engage and influence senior state officials.
Deep understanding of state education policy, accountability systems, and governance structures.
Proven experience translating complex policy landscapes into strategic organizational action.
Exceptional communication skills, especially in executive-level environments.
Ability to travel frequently (approx. 30%) and manage executive relationships across multiple states.
Ability to gain and apply in depth product knowledge of ACT’s products and services, including how the products and services are collectively used to provide solutions to state customers.
Demonstrated ability to influence and engage key state executives.
Ability to gather and use competitive intelligence to create strategies that advance and/or protect ACT’s interests.
Ability to work effectively and build relationships with individuals within the organization.
Strong communication skills including ability to communicate effectively across all levels in the organization, as well as outstanding presentation skills.
Strong analytical abilities and the ability to determine logical solutions to complicated problems.
Ability to set goals and priorities and manage to completion.
Strong negotiation skills.
Skills and knowledge required for success in this position attained through experience and education (Bachelor’s degree in Education, Business, or related area of study), or a combination of both.

It’s a Plus If You Have

Assessment industry experience.
Account management or sales experience.
Previous experience and demonstrated success leading, managing, and building teams.

About ACT

When ACT was founded in 1959, it disrupted the assessment industry with a new approach to helping students better understand their readiness so they could take steps to improve it. By leveraging our expertise and authority in assessment and research, we will again disrupt the industry—helping more people learn, better measure their progress, and improve their navigation through life’s transitions.

More than ever before, ACT is fulfilling its mission of helping people achieve education and workplace success. We’re doing it by pushing the boundaries of learning innovation through the work of our people, who we call team members because we’re all in this together.

We know transformation does not come without challenge. That’s why ACT invests in a variety of experiences for team members to strengthen their connections, explore ideas, learn from customers, and celebrate success.

Learn more about working at ACT at act.org!
